finding.claim: _validate_sub fails open: when the caller pins subject= and the token omits the sub claim, the subject check is skipped and the token is accepted.
finding.source: Attacker holds a validly signed token from the same issuer/key that lacks a sub claim (precondition; signature still verified).
finding.sink: Subject-binding check in _validate_sub (api_jwt.py:452-454), never reached when sub is absent.

trace.note: _validate_claims calls _validate_sub(payload, subject) when verify_sub is set.
_validate_sub begins; line 446-447 returns early if 'sub' not in payload.
Expected-subject comparison only runs when sub is present.

finding.guards_checked: verify_sub defaults on; signature verification runs first. Sibling validators _validate_iss (api_jwt.py:571-572) and _validate_aud (api_jwt.py:529-532) raise MissingRequiredClaimError when the caller requires the claim, so this is inconsistent. Upstream PyJWT may intend this behavior; not confirmable from this copy (no tests/docs present). Not reproduced by execution.

finding.claim: With cache_jwk_set=False, an unverified token's kid drives two unthrottled outbound JWKS fetches per call, serialized under _client_lock, enabling request amplification and thread stalls.
finding.source: kid header of an unauthenticated token, read by get_signing_key_from_jwt with verify_signature disabled (jwks_client.py:280-282).
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP in fetch_data (jwks_client.py:156-163), invoked from get_signing_keys (line 247) and get_signing_keys(refresh=True) (line 258) while holding _client_lock (line 246).

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt passes unverified kid to get_signing_key.
get_signing_keys() -> get_jwk_set(): cache is None so fetch_data runs (fetch #1).
cooling_down requires jwk_set_cache is not None, so it is False when the cache is disabled.
Unknown kid triggers get_signing_keys(refresh=True): fetch #2, no cooldown.

finding.guards_checked: Cooldown applies only when the JWK set cache is enabled (documented in docstring). No rate limit. URI scheme check (jwks_client.py:105-110) does not limit volume. Timeout 30s per fetch, held under RLock. Not reproduced by execution.

finding.claim: cache_keys=True caches signing keys per kid with no time-based expiry, so a key removed from the JWKS (rotated out or revoked) keeps verifying tokens in-process until LRU eviction.
finding.source: Attacker holds the private key of a key that was removed from the JWKS (precondition; no JWKS write access needed).
finding.sink: Cached PyJWK returned from get_signing_key and used for signature verification (jwks_client.py:267).

trace.note: get_signing_key wrapped in lru_cache(maxsize=max_cached_keys) when cache_keys is True.
First successful lookup is returned and cached; later JWKS removal does not evict it.

finding.guards_checked: Behavior is documented in the class docstring (lines 69-72). Cache disabled by default. Revocation gap rather than auth bypass. Not reproduced by execution.

finding.claim: Time-claim validators catch only ValueError, so non-numeric or infinite exp/nbf/iat values raise TypeError/OverflowError instead of InvalidTokenError.
finding.source: Time claim (exp, nbf, or iat) set to null, a list, or 1e400 (inf) in a token body.
finding.guards_checked: Requires a validly signed token, or verify_signature disabled with time checks explicitly enabled; default merge disables these (api_jwt.py:81-89). Effect is an uncaught exception / 500, not an auth bypass.
